The refractive index of water while compared to with glass

$$\frac{n_1}{n_2} = \frac{\sin \theta_2}{\sin \theta_1} = 0.88$$

which is less than $1$.

You therefore divide the refractive index of the medium that you want to determine by the refractive index of the medium with respect to which you want to determine the refractive index.

Diamond with respect to water : $1.82$
Water with respect to diamond : $0.55$
Diamond with respect to glass : $1.59$
Glass with respect to diamond : $0.63$

But in physics usually the refractive index of a particular substance is used, not the refractive index of one substance in comparison to another.

When discussing reflection, we learned that when perfect and total reflection is needed, then instead of mirror a perfect transparent medium is used, and a kind of reflection is made. This is called total internal reflection. It is a very easy and exciting process. Here, light rays are sent to a rarer medium from a denser medium using the refraction of light. We know (and have used many times) that the law of refraction is $n_1 \sin \theta_1 = n_2 \sin \theta_2$ i.e if $n_2$ is greater than $n_1$ then $\theta_1$ is greater than $\theta_2$.

Suppose you are sending a ray of light from a denser ($n_2$) medium to a rarer ($n_1$) medium (Fig 9.05). According to the laws of reflection and refraction some amount of light will be reflected and some will be refracted. As $\theta_2$ will be greater than $\theta_1$ therefore staying $\theta_2$ ($90^\circ$, $\theta_1$ will be equal to $90^\circ$ and after this there will be no scope of light to be refracted, i.e when $\theta_2$ will be equal to $90^\circ$, total light has to be reflected. The value of $\theta_1$ at which $\theta_2 = 90^\circ$ is called the critical angle $\theta_c$.
